0:0.en: My name is Wang Ming, I am a student, and I live in Beijing.

0:1.en: There are three people in my family: Dad, Mom, and me.

1:0.en: Today is Saturday, I am not going to school.

1:1.en: In the morning I read books at home, and Mom cooked.

1:2.en: At noon we eat rice and dishes; the dishes Mom made are very delicious.

2:0.en: In the afternoon, my friend and I went to the store to buy things.

2:1.en: I bought some apples, and my friend bought a cup.

1:2.en: It rained today, and it's a bit cold.

2:0.en: I live at a friend's house.

1:1.en: Shanghai is big, there are many people.

2:1.en: Her home is very beautiful; there is a small shop in front of it.

2:2.en: Her kitten is named "Rice", and I really like it.

3:0.en: When are you coming to Shanghai?

3:1.en: I want to treat you to dinner; shall we go watch a movie together?

0:1.en: Chengdu mornings aren't very cold, and there are many people in the market.

1:0.en: Mom wants to buy fish and eggs.

0:0.en: On Sunday morning, my mom and I went to the vegetable market near our home.

1:1.en: The fish-selling auntie smiled and said: "The fish today are very good, I'll sell them cheaply to you!"

1:4.en: Mom thought it was a bit expensive, but because the fish was good, she still bought one.

2:1.en: The fruit-selling uncle let me eat a small piece first, it's really sweet!

卖水果的叔叔.say: mài shuǐ guǒ de shū shu

2:2.en: We bought a big watermelon, but it was too heavy.

2:3.en: On the way home, I walked very slowly, and Mom walked faster than me.

2:4.en: When I got home, I was so tired I didn't want to talk, I just wanted to eat watermelon.

0:0.en: Last night, I was busy at the company until nine o'clock before I got off work.

0:1.en: After getting on the bus, I wanted to call my wife, but I couldn't find my cell phone.

1:0.en: I searched my pockets and my bag, but found nothing.

1:1.en: I think: the cell phone might still be on the desk at the company.

1:2.en: I got off the car immediately and ran back to the company.

2:0.en: The office door is already closed.

2:2.en: I said: "I am looking for my cell phone, but it's too dark here, I can't see anything."

3:0.en: He laughed: “Isn't that a cell phone in your hand?”

2:1.en: Just as I didn't know what to do, someone beside me asked, "Sir, what are you looking for?"

3:1.en: As soon as I looked, my phone really was in my hand, and its screen was still on.

0:1.en: How have you been feeling lately?

0:2.en: I have been in Taipei for three months already; I've always wanted to write you a letter, but there's too much schoolwork, and only today do I have time.

1:0.en: Winter in Taipei isn't cold at all; it's completely different from our northern region.

1:1.en: It often rains here, so there is always an umbrella in my bag.

1:2.en: The place where I live is very close to the school; it takes ten minutes by bicycle to get there.

1:3.en: There is a night market nearby; it's lively and cheap, and I love the beef noodles there the most.

1:4.en: To be honest, they still aren't as delicious as the dumplings you make.

2:0.en: When I first arrived here, I couldn't understand some of the words people here said, for example they call 'potato' 'ma ling shu', and call 'bicycle' 'jiao ta che'.

2:1.en: Now I've gradually gotten used to it, and I've also made several new friends.

3:0.en: Grandma, please take care of your health and don't get too tired.

3:1.en: Once the vacation starts, I will definitely go back to visit you and bring you tea from Taiwan.

0:0.en: Last weekend, I took my grandpa to a famous restaurant in Shanghai to eat.

0:1.en: After sitting down, we waited for a long time, but no waiter brought us a menu.

0:2.en: Later I discovered that there was a QR code on the table, and customers needed to use their phones to order food themselves.

1:0.en: For me, this is very convenient: no waiting, no need to shout at the waiter, and the photos of the dishes are very clear.

1:2.en: His eyesight is poor, the text on his phone is too small, and he can't see clearly.

1:1.en: But grandpa is not very happy.

2:0.en: I think what Grandpa said makes sense.

1:3.en: He said: "In the past, when ordering food, you could ask the waiter which dish was delicious, but now you can only ask your phone."

2:1.en: Although the new method is fast and convenient, it may not be suitable for everyone.

2:3.en: Actually, besides having good food, a good restaurant should also make every guest feel comfortable.

2:2.en: Restaurants should let customers choose for themselves: young people who are willing to use mobile phones can use mobile phones, and elderly people who want to look at menus should also have menus available.

0:0.en: Recently, a special bookshelf appeared in an old hutong in Beijing's Dongcheng District.

1:0.en: The owner of the bookshelf is retired teacher Zhao Jianguo, who is sixty-eight years old this year.

0:1.en: It stands under an old locust tree, unattended and requiring no paperwork; residents can take books at any time, with only one condition: put them back after reading, or replace them with one of your own books.

1:2.en: At first, the family worried that the books would soon be taken away completely.

1:3.en: However, three months passed, and not only did the books on the bookshelf not decrease, but instead they increased from the original forty to over two hundred.

1:1.en: He told reporters that after retirement, the books at home kept piling up, and rather than letting them gather dust in the cabinet, it would be better to take them out and share them with the neighbors.

2:0.en: Nowadays, this bookshelf has become one of the liveliest places in the hutong.

2:1.en: In the early evening, you can often see children sitting under trees reading comics, while old people drink tea and discuss historical novels at the same time.

3:0.en: Regarding this phenomenon, community staff stated that they plan to promote similar practices in several other hutongs.

社区工作人员.say: shè qū gōng zuò rén yuán

2:2.en: Xiao Chen, a college student who lives nearby, said she originally just passed by, but later became a regular here, and even voluntarily took charge of organizing the books once a week.

3:1.en: Zhao Jianguo then said it even more simply: “A book only counts as a real book once someone has read it.”

0:1.en: Bamboo chairs, lidded bowls, a pot of boiling water, plus the rising and falling sound of conversation and laughter, make up the most common scenery in this city.

0:2.en: When I first arrived, I strongly disapproved of this: spending an entire afternoon doing nothing but sitting and drinking tea—wasn't that wasting time?

1:0.en: Back then, I had just transferred from Shanghai and was used to a fast-paced life of racing against time; even my walking was half a beat faster than others.

1:1.en: In my opinion, time is efficiency, efficiency is everything.

0:0.en: People who have lived in Chengdu are probably not unfamiliar with teahouses.

1:2.en: Only when one day, an old tea guest over seventy years old slowly told me: "Young man, tea must be brewed slowly, for the flavor to come out."

1:4.en: At that time I just smiled politely and didn't take it to heart.

2:1.en: In the teahouse, no one rushes you, and no one cares about your title.

2:2.en: Strangers can chat for hours about anything under the sun; meeting by chance, yet there is no barrier between them.

2:0.en: However, after a long time, I gradually realized the weight of this sentence.

2:3.en: The time I once thought was wasted was actually quietly nourishing trust between people and allowing an anxious heart to settle.

3:0.en: Nowadays, the fast-paced life has swept through every city, Chengdu is no exception, and delivery riders still hurry past teahouse doors.

3:1.en: But I have always believed that a society's maturity lies not in how fast everyone runs, but in whether there is still a place for 'slowness'.

3:2.en: After all, seeking quick success and instant benefit may bring temporary results, but only proceeding calmly and unhurriedly can lead to lasting success.
